sections.h2: One government for tax, value and deeds
sections.html:
Broomfield sits between Denver and Boulder along US 36 and US 287, and it is a city and a county at once. Its own Assessor, Treasurer and Clerk and Recorder all work from One DesCombes Drive, inside the George Di Ciero City and County Building. A single government values the house, mails the bill and files the deed.

Phone the Treasurer at 303-464-5810 or the Assessor at 303-464-5819, or email assessor@broomfield.org.

The city dates from 1961, and the county was created by consolidation on November 15, 2001, using land from four counties. That date matters for old records: the online recording portal starts with documents recorded in November 2001, and anything earlier may be held in Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld.

The 2020 count was 74,112 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 79,174, within 32.97 square miles. Owner-occupants live in 62.7% of homes, the median owner-occupied home is valued at $664,500, and median gross rent is $2,126. Because six school districts reach into the city, your address decides which mill levy lands on your bill, and neighbors a mile apart can pay different amounts.

Plan on three dates: February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second, and April 30 if you pay everything at once. Pay on or before them and there is no interest.

Notices are sent to the owner of record, not the mortgage company, around the third week of January by email or mail. A lender that pays from escrow should be asked to confirm. When the tax is under $25, only the full-tax option is available.

Payment optionDue dateLate interest
First halfFebruary 281% in March, rising to 10% in December
Second halfJune 151% in late June, rising to 7% in December
Full paymentApril 301% in May, rising to 8% in December

After a due date, call 303-438-6390 for updated figures.

Payment can be made in cash, by check, by eCheck or by credit card. The card vendor adds 2.50% and an eCheck costs $2.50. Each online transaction is capped at $1,000,000.

Seniors can apply for tax deferral at colorado.propertytaxdeferral.com. Separately, a Certificate of Taxes Due (C.R.S. 39-10-115) states that every tax is paid apart from items it lists as still owed. Ask your title company whether it will order one for your sale.

Values are reset in odd-numbered years and carried forward through even ones unless the property changes. January 1 is the assessment date.

For the 2025 and 2026 reappraisals, the Assessor looks at residential sales between July 1, 2022 and June 30, 2024, counting only qualified arms-length sales. Homes are valued by the market approach under USPAP guidelines.

In an even year a notice arrives only after a change such as a finished basement, an addition or a demolition. Your tax is value times assessment rate times mill levy, where the legislature fixes the assessment rate and the taxing authorities set the levy.

Real property protests go to the Assessor from May 1 to June 8. For personal property, the cutoff is June 30.

  • Online: the appeal portal at appeals.spatialest.com/co-broomfield, which includes a neighborhood sales map and document uploads.
  • Mail: the Real Property Protest Form, postmarked by June 8, to PO Box 1149, Broomfield, CO 80038-1149.
  • In person: the Community Assistance Center in the main lobby of the City and County Building.

Useful evidence includes an appraisal dated 7/1/2022 to 6/30/2024, photos of condition, comparable sales and proof of record errors. A Notice of Determination is sent by June 30 for real property.

Disagree with the result? The Board of Equalization takes real property appeals until July 15 and personal property appeals until July 20. Hearings are remote, before an independent hearing officer, and the burden is on you to show that your value is the more accurate one. Evidence files must be 20 MB or smaller. The board's contact is clk-boe@broomfield.org or 303-438-6332, option 9. Hearings run in late July and finish by August 5.

A flat $43 covers the first page of any recorded document under the schedule effective June 1, 2026, and added pages cost nothing. The city's recording page breaks that into a $40 fee and a $3 surcharge per document.

The documentary fee adds $0.01 per $100 of consideration over $500, and Treasurer's, public trustee's and sheriff's deeds are exempt. Recording staff work weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. You can mail, drop off, deliver or e-record.

Documents need a one-inch top and bottom margin and half-inch side margins, a return address and a signed check payable to the City and County of Broomfield. The office cannot give legal advice on which document to file.

sections.h2: Preparing the paperwork before you sell
sections.html:
A little organizing up front helps. Pull the last tax statement, the notice of value and any protest decision, and write down who pays the tax, you or your lender through escrow. Then call the Treasurer and ask for the current balance and for the interest that would apply if closing slips into the next month.

Next, check the recording side. The Recording Division wants a one-inch top and bottom margin, a return address and a signed check, so any deed you sign yourself should meet those formatting rules before it goes in. Most sellers never do this alone, because the title company files the deed, but it is good to know what the office will check.

Last, think about timing. A sale that closes between the February and June dates will have one half already paid, so the settlement statement should show a credit or a charge for the part of the year each side owns. Ask your closing agent to explain how that split was calculated.

Any property tax you still owe is paid by the title company out of your proceeds. Get current numbers from the Treasurer before picking a date, since interest grows each month. If you close in late winter, check whether the February first half has been paid.

Gather your last tax statement, your notice of value and the name of your lender if taxes are escrowed. If you pay your own taxes, make sure the owner-of-record address is current. With a cash buyer, you can skip the loan approval step, and the title company only needs the payoff and the deed to finish. That keeps the closing date in your hands, which helps when you are relocating or settling an estate on a deadline.

faqs.q: When are Broomfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second, April 30 for one full payment. A missed date brings 1% interest the next month.

faqs.q: Does Broomfield have a separate county government?
faqs.a: Yes. Broomfield became a consolidated city and county on November 15, 2001, so one government assesses, bills and records.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Broomfield valuation?
faqs.a: June 8 for real property. A Board of Equalization appeal comes next, due July 15.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Broomfield?
faqs.a: Recording is a flat $43 per document under the June 1, 2026 schedule. The documentary fee, $0.01 per $100 above $500, is added to that.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Broomfield house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent settles the balance from your proceeds. For the exact amount, call the Treasurer at 303-464-5810 or 303-438-6390.
